samples.summary: Color-reset test cannot distinguish `{ color: undefined }` from `{}` — the exact distinction the fix depends on
samples.evidence: `expect(editor.applyStyle).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ color: undefined })` (and the `backgroundColor` twin at line 87) uses jest/vitest recursive equality, which treats an explicitly-`undefined` property as equal to an absent one — `expect({}).toEqual({color: undefined})` passes. The whole point of the change is that the key must be PRESENT with value `undefined`, because the store's clear path keys off `key in style && style[key] === undefined` (see `removedCellStyleAttrs` in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:248 and `removedInlineStyleAttrs` at :148). A regression that passed `{}` (key dropped) would leave the stale attribute on the CRDT node and still pass this test. The test does catch the old `""` behavior, so it is not fully vacuous, but it does not cover the property it claims to. A `Object.keys(call[0])` / `'color' in call[0]` assertion would close it.

samples.summary: The setBlockType node-scoped removal (removeStyleByPath → removeNodeStyle) has no test for the subtree case it was changed for
samples.evidence: The comment at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1455-1459 states the change matters because on a *table* block the old path range would strip `listKind`/`listLevel`/`headingLevel` from every block nested in its cells. The diff adds subtree-safety tests for `applyCellStyle` ('should not strip backgroundColor from nodes inside the cell') and `applyCellSpan` ('should clear colSpan in the CRDT without touching nested cells'), but the equivalent test for `setBlockType` is absent: the only stale-attribute test is 'should remove stale listKind/listLevel from tree when changing to paragraph' (tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:1910) on a plain paragraph block, which passes identically under the old range-based removal. So this third call site's behavior change is uncovered.
searchedFor: read the new 'block style codec' and applyCellSpan describe blocks in the diff

samples.summary: New inline validation: only the `text` branch is tested; the `not an object` and `'style' must be an object` branches have no test
samples.evidence: The new inline loop adds three rejections (controller.ts:406 not-an-object, :412 text-must-be-string, :417 style-must-be-object). Only the second is covered — spec.ts:532 'rejects a malformed inline' with `inlines: [{ text: 5 }]`. Nothing sends `inlines: [null]` or `inlines: [{ text: 'x' }]` (missing style), so the newly-added, newly-*breaking* requirement that every inline carry a `style` object is entirely unexercised; deleting that check would not fail any test.
searchedFor: grep "'style' must be an object" in packages/backend/src/api/v1

samples.summary: The docs-table-inside-slide-text-body recursion in assertValidTextBodyBlocks is untested
samples.evidence: `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` recurses through `block.tableData.rows[r].cells[c]` (controller.ts:604-616) to validate block styles of a docs table nested inside a slide text body. Every new slides-arm test in the spec (spec.ts:746-868) targets `data.blocks`, `data.text.blocks`, the slides table element's `data.rows[].cells[].body`, or a group child — none of them nests a docs `tableData` inside a slide text body, so this recursive branch (and its path string `…blocks[i].tableData.rows[r].cells[c]`) is never executed. Likewise the `'blocks' must be an array` (controller.ts:583) and `assertValidTextBody` 'text body must be an object' (controller.ts:567) branches have no test.

samples.summary: removedCellStyleAttrs lists 7 clearable keys; only backgroundColor is tested
samples.evidence: `removedCellStyleAttrs` covers `backgroundColor, verticalAlign, padding, borderTop/Bottom/Left/Right`, but the two new tests ('should clear the fill in the CRDT when backgroundColor is undefined' and 'should not strip backgroundColor from nodes inside the cell', tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts around :2033) only exercise `backgroundColor`; `verticalAlign` appears only as the untouched-key assertion. Clearing a border or padding via explicit `undefined` — the same reset mechanism — is uncovered.

samples.summary: New shared codec has no direct unit test; the write-side drop of an invalid alignment / non-finite number is never exercised
samples.evidence: There is no packages/docs/test/model/crdt-attrs.test.ts (glob 'packages/docs/test/model/crdt*' returns nothing). Coverage is only indirect via backend docs-tree.spec.ts and frontend yorkie-doc-store.test.ts, and both only write a *fully empty* style (`style: {}`). `serializeBlockStyleAttrs` dropping a present-but-invalid value — e.g. `alignment: 'bogus'` or `marginTop: NaN`/`Infinity` — is not covered anywhere, nor is round-trip symmetry serialize→parse for a populated style.

verdict.reason: Verified all claims. color-reset.test.ts:81 and :87 assert exactly as quoted via toHaveBeenCalledWith({color: undefined}) / ({backgroundColor: undefined}). The store's clear path genuinely keys off property PRESENCE: yorkie-doc-store.ts:151 `if (key in style && style[key] === undefined)` with clear('color') at :161 and clear('backgroundColor') at :162; the cell twin at :255 uses the same filter. The doc comment at :140-147 confirms that a dropped key makes styleByPath silently keep the stale value on the Tree node. The component (text-format-group.tsx:130/:315 shorthand, reset wired at :252/:347) would emit `{}` under a regression that conditionally builds the payload, and vitest's toHaveBeenCalledWith uses toEqual-style non-strict equality that treats an undefined-valued key as equal to an absent one — so that regression class passes the test. No compensating strictness: tests/setup.ts adds no custom equality testers, package.json:107 pins vitest ^4.1.8 with no toStrictEqual anywhere in the file. No other test closes the gap: color-picker-grid.test.ts:61-66 only asserts onReset was called and never inspects the payload, and yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:648-667 supplies the explicit-undefined keys itself so it exercises the store, not the component's payload shape. Real, in-lane (assertion holds regardless of the specific property the fix depends on), and blocking.
